lecture_title: Fourier Duality, Momentum, and Free-Particle Motion

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_01.png
assets.rationale: The settled board records the singlet-triplet decomposition and photon-field states used in the opening carryover discussion.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: times no photon and one photon

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: Both directions of the symmetric Fourier transform pair are complete and legible.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the basic theorem of Fourier analysis

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: The delta sampling identity is isolated without unrelated board clutter.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the delta function is only non-zero

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: The boxed Fourier kernel and its identification with a delta distribution are visible at the decisive derivation step.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: It is just a good old delta function
assets.caption_hint: Fourier kernel identified as a delta distribution

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: The continuous position-basis expansion and recovery of its coefficient by projection are complete.

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: Continuous orthogonality and the wave-function inner product appear together in their original board sequence.
assets.caption_hint: Continuous basis normalization and inner product

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: Multiplication by position acting on a delta-localized state is fully visible.
assets.caption_hint: Delta distribution as a position eigenfunction

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: The plane-wave solution of the momentum eigenvalue equation is cleanly isolated.

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_09.png
assets.rationale: Projection onto a momentum eigenket visibly becomes the Fourier transform of the position-space wave function.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: wave function in the momentum basis

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_10.png
assets.rationale: The time-dependent Schrodinger equation and the choice H=cP are legible at the dynamics pivot.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: wave functions in the x basis
assets.caption_hint: Schrodinger evolution with a linear Hamiltonian

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_11.png
assets.rationale: The first-order transport equation is complete and supports the rigid-translation solution.

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_12.png
assets.rationale: Hamilton's equations for H=cp are complete, with constant velocity and conserved momentum shown together.

assets.name: lecture_09_figure_13.png
assets.rationale: The free-particle Schrodinger equation obtained from P squared over 2m is complete and unobstructed.
